surface_forms: le prince allemand qu'était M. de Charlus
une dame qui vint me dire bonjour

appraisal_events.evidence: Posted at the head of the great staircase with admirers around him, «les invités [...] étaient forcés de venir lui dire bonsoir»; the princesse omits her own friends «à sa crainte de mécontenter "Palamède" qui les avait excommuniés»; «M. de Charlus savait qu'il était un Guermantes occupant une place prépondérante dans cette fête», picturing himself as the Margrave of Tannhäuser.
appraisal_events.explanation: The passage installs Charlus as the real gatekeeper of the party — even the hostess defers to his exclusions and every guest must file past him — so his local standing rises sharply, while the «glapissement continu», the «ton radouci, factice» and the operatic self-image keep the elevation comically framed rather than admiring.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme de Souvré pushes him toward the prince «d'un mouvement prétendu protecteur et volontairement inefficace qui me laissa en panne presque à mon point de départ. Telle est la lâcheté des gens du monde.»; then «Mme d'Arpajon fut plus lâche encore que Mme de Souvré», answering his request with an angry silence meant as «une leçon muette».
appraisal_events.explanation: Twice refused an introduction to the host, the narrator is left stranded outside the party's inner circle; the narrator's own verdict of «lâcheté» simultaneously discredits the two women who withhold the favor, Mme d'Arpajon the more so as the text exposes her dwindling credit and her replacement by Mme de Surgis.

status_effects.explanation: He is shown as the party's obligatory passage point and as a power the princesse herself will not cross, which is the strongest local elevation in the passage.
Both attempts to be presented to the prince fail, leaving him unadmitted and roughly where he started.
Her double-edged gesture — appearing to recommend while ensuring nothing happens — is named outright as worldly cowardice.
She is ranked as even more cowardly than Mme de Souvré, and her pretended deafness and visible scowl are narrated as naive and ungracious.

The same movement spells out her collapse of credit: little power to begin with, weakened by her liaison with the duc de Guermantes, finished by his abandonment, and sealed by the sight of Mme de Surgis who has replaced her.
The closing image raises her at Mme d'Arpajon's expense: all eyes turn to her, statue-like and «magnifique», as Basin's new favorite.

ambiguities: In «demander de me présenter à M. de Guermantes», the surface form «M. de Guermantes» denotes the evening's host, the prince de Guermantes, not the duc; the duc appears separately in the passage as «Basin de Guermantes». Mapping this form to the duc would misassign the snub.

The Charlus tableau is genuinely double-edged: the mocking notation of his «glapissement continu», his «ton radouci, factice» and his Tannhäuser self-flattery could support reading the paragraph as comic diminishment rather than elevation. It is read here as elevation because the narrator states his «place prépondérante» as fact and shows the hostess and every guest actually submitting to it.
